_comment: Wave 2: product direction - local shops, pricing, competitors, design. Each is grounded in a finding or a verified external source.

tasks.title: Local shop directory from the ATF FFL licensee list
tasks.why: The owner asked for a location function so users can find nearby gun shops for ammo and reloading supplies. This is the cheapest and most authoritative source available, and it is free: the ATF publishes a complete, PUBLIC DOMAIN listing of every federal firearms licensee in the US, updated MONTHLY, with name, street address, city, state, zip, and a licence type that separates a dealer (01), a pawnbroker (02) and a RELOADER (06). That last one is the key: type 06 is legally a reloading business, a far better filter for this site than any hand-assembled directory. Verified at catalog.data.gov dataset 4092, publisher ATF Open Data, accessLevel public, accrualPeriodicity R/P1M, contact atfopendata@atf.gov.
tasks.evidence: A numbers product's most important design decision is how it renders we do not know. This project's dominant data state is absent: six dimensional columns are 0/229 populated. A design that has no vocabulary for absence renders a blank cell, and a blank cell is read as 0.
scope: Fetch and profile the ATF FFL dataset. Report the EXACT schema: every column name, the licence type codes and their meanings, and the row count. Do not summarise from the catalogue page - download the file and read it.

Determine which licence types are relevant. Type 06 (reloader) is the strongest signal for reloading supplies; 01 (dealer) covers retail; 02 (pawnbroker) implies some gunsmithing. Say what each implies and what it does NOT - a 01 does not necessarily sell ammunition, and an 06 does not necessarily have a storefront.

State the staleness honestly. The catalogue entry lists December 2021 data with a September 2025 update timestamp. Determine the real currency of the file before anything depends on it, because a shop that closed two years ago is worse than no shop.

Establish the licence position explicitly. It is a US federal government work in the public domain, but record the attribution requirement and any restriction ATF states, because we still cite the source.

Specify the geographic index. The owner asked for a location lookup, so state whether the data carries latitude/longitude or is street address only. That decides whether distance-sort is possible at all, and it must be answered before any design is proposed.
Design the data model for a local shop record, including what we do NOT know and how absence is marked. A shop with no recorded hours must not render as open 24 hours.
do_not: Do not build the feature. Produce the specification, the schema report and the licence position. A human implements.
Do not scrape or geocode anything. Reading the file the publisher provides is not scraping.

Do not add a storefront, phone or hours field from any source other than this dataset. If hours are found elsewhere, record them as a separate clearly-labelled source - never merge unverified attributes into an authoritative record.
Do not claim a listed business currently sells ammunition. The FFL list says a licence exists, not what is on the shelf.

tasks.title: How to get retailer pricing - feeds, APIs, and why not scraping
tasks.why: The owner asked for scripts that search vendor websites so the site can display what they have and at what price. That goal is legitimate but the obvious implementation - scrape the storefronts - is the wrong one and probably unlawful. This task finds the lawful routes and prices them. It matters that our own retailers.js already reasons carefully about FTC endorsement rules, so a pricing feature must not undo that work.
tasks.evidence: That combination is the single highest-risk thing on the site, for reasons that have nothing to do with taste: FTC Endorsement Guides (16 CFR 255.5) require a material connection to be disclosed, but disclosure only cures an endorsement; it does not make an unsupported endorsement true.
scope: Research the lawful routes and say what each costs and requires. Known to exist: AmmoSeek publishes a public XML feed specification for retailers and runs an affiliate network; Gunfinder and DOPE both publish feed specifications; Impact, Awin and AvantLink are affiliate networks carrying firearms-adjacent merchants. For each state: what data it gives, whether price and stock are included, the cost to join, and whether it needs the merchant's participation.

State the terms-of-service position on scraping retailer storefronts, concretely and with sources. ToS is not scraping etiquette - a site that prohibits automated access in its ToS is prohibiting it in law in most jurisdictions. Include the CFAA and hiQ v LinkedIn, and state plainly whether a retailer can revoke permission for content we link to commercially.

Quantify staleness, because it is the strongest technical argument against scraping and the owner should see a number not an opinion. A scraped price is a snapshot. How long is it true? What does a price look like to a user an hour, a day and a week after capture? What must the UI say for a price of unknown age not to mislead?
Assess the affiliate-network route as the recommended path and state what we give up: commissions, and dependency on one intermediary. Say whether a zero-cost route exists.
Recommend ONE approach with reasoning, and state what would change the recommendation. A recommendation without a falsifier is an opinion.
do_not: Do not write a scraper. Do not fetch a retailer storefront to test whether scraping works - that is the action this task exists to evaluate, and doing it to find out would repeat the mistake.
Do not give legal advice. Cite what the terms say and what the case law holds; say plainly when it is unsettled.
Do not recommend a price display until the staleness and ToS questions are answered. A price shown without provenance and age is a claim we cannot substantiate.

tasks.title: Competitor teardown - features we lack
tasks.why: The owner asked what competitors are doing that we are not. We have partial coverage: ammoseek-coverage compared cartridge NAME coverage and found 36.30 percent of their search share is already held by us. That compared names. Nobody has compared features, calculators or the shopping experience.
tasks.evidence: Only naive string matching produces the brief's answer. Always alias-normalise before claiming a caliber gap. This took a ten-line script.
scope: Enumerate the competitors. AmmoSeek is already studied for coverage; find the others - gun.deals, gunammo.deals, FIREARMSDATA, reloadus, AmmoReady and whatever else carries real traffic. Record each URL and the date observed.

For each, list what they offer that we do not, ranked by how much a user would care. Distinguish a genuine capability from a presentation difference - a prettier page is not a feature, and a feature we have but present worse is a different fix.
State what THEY lack that we have, and say so plainly. A teardown that only finds gaps is marketing, not research, and it would mislead the owner into thinking we are behind.
For the top five gaps, give a rough effort estimate and the write-set each would touch, so the owner can approve a batch the way the low-risk fixes were approved.
do_not: Do not copy a competitor's design, copy, code or layout. Record what capability exists and what problem it solves. We build our own expression of it.
Do not scrape a competitor to measure anything. Read what they publish.
Do not rank by what is easiest for us to build. Rank by what a user would actually notice missing.

tasks.title: Apply the accumulated UI findings to the live site
tasks.why: ui-research produced a specific, verified list of defects and none are fixed, because agents cannot edit the application. Four are concrete enough to act on and none need a design decision to settle.
tasks.evidence: The affiliate disclosure currently lives in a permanent top bar and in the footer. Neither is where the decision happens. A reader choosing a retailer should see that retailer is an affiliate on the card, next to the button. A disclosure the reader must scroll back to find is not a disclosure.
scope: Produce a concrete diff for each of the four verified defects: move affiliate disclosure onto the retailer card adjacent to the link; add font-variant-numeric tabular-nums to live numeric fields, noting docs/mockups/_tokens.css line 17 already has it and was never ported; split the accent so action and positive-status are never the same token; and replace any em-dash unknown marker with a word.
State precisely where each change goes, by file and line, so it can be applied without re-deriving the analysis.

Re-run the CSP grep against your own proposed diff before submitting it. The original task's grep found 19 violations in the author's OWN first draft - inline style= attributes written while styling quickly. A check that passed on someone else's artefact failed on the one just made, and it will fail on yours.
do_not: Do not edit apps/website/. Produce diffs. Same rule as every other research task.
Do not introduce an inline style attribute, a new remote origin or an icon font. The site is one self-contained HTML file under a strict CSP, and the CSP constraint is why the design is coherent.
Do not redesign anything not on the list. This is a defect sweep, not a redesign.
